geometryPolicy: Authority-table points are used when surviving evidence does not support a defensible territorial boundary. These records must not be promoted to the possessions layer.

representations.label: Venetian Quarter, Constantinople
representations.rationale: The quarter changed jurisdiction and extent across three authority phases, while the available sources do not establish a parcel boundary precise enough for a polygon. The phased point records preserve those changes without implying cadastral certainty.

representations.label: Venetian fondaco at Tana
representations.rationale: Tana was a trading post under Golden Horde suzerainty, not a territorial possession. A port-authority point communicates presence and chronology without turning the fondaco into a sovereign enclave.

representations.label: Venetian commercial presence at Trebizond
representations.rationale: The evidence supports a Venetian commercial presence inside the Empire of Trebizond but not a stable, surveyable quarter boundary. The foreign-port authority record is therefore the published representation.
